round_selection: Prefix rounds 0 through 1, inclusive, of the deployed R_F=8/R_P=56 schedule, in which rounds 0 to 3 and 60 to 63 are full and rounds 4 to 59 are partial. Round i uses deployed round-constant row i and the deployed MDS matrix; constants are never regenerated for a reduced instance. Rounds 0 and 1 are both full rounds: add constants to all three state elements, apply x^5 to all three, then multiply by the MDS matrix.
message_domain: Exactly 64 bytes: two 32-byte little-endian Pallas base field elements, each strictly less than p = 0x40000000000000000000000000000000224698fc094cf91b992d30ed00000001. Non-canonical encodings are rejected, so an element encoding x + p is not a valid message even though it is congruent to x. Any other length is rejected.

relation.postcondition: The two output field elements are equal (equivalently, identical 32-byte canonical encodings).

out_of_scope: Changing rounds, constants, capacity element, mode or output length
selection_note: Organizer-selected exploration target; no first-unbroken boundary is asserted.
constants: The 192 deployed round constants (64 rows of 3) and the deployed 3x3 MDS matrix from halo2_poseidon 0.2.0, halo2_poseidon/src/fp.rs, reproducible with the Poseidon v1.1 reference generator as recorded in that file. A reduced instance keeps the first r rows unchanged.
padding: None at this length. The deployed ConstantLength<2> domain pads with zeros to a multiple of the rate, and two elements already fill one rate block, so no padding element is absorbed.
initialization: Initial state [m0, m1, 2^65]. The capacity element is L * 2^64 with L = 2 and a hard-coded output length of 1, encoding the constant input length as the Poseidon authors specify.
schedule: One permutation over the whole message. Each round adds its constants to all three elements, applies the S-box (to all three in a full round, to element 0 only in a partial round), then multiplies the state by the MDS matrix.
feed_forward: None. This is a sponge with a fixed capacity element, not a Davies-Meyer construction.
digest_encoding: State element 0 after the selected rounds, as 32 little-endian bytes. The output space is p, about 2^254, not 2^256, so the generic collision exponent is about 127.
nominal_security_note: The nominal reference for this target is 127, not the 128 used for binary 256-bit targets, because the output space is the field order rather than the full digest encoding.
